name: Motion sensors
author: Bench Workshop
description: Sensors that feel how they move and which way they face: a tilt switch, a compass (QMC5883L, as on the GY-271) and an ADXL345 accelerometer. They feel the real motion of whatever they're glued to: pick it up with the hand and tilt it. Also sketch libraries for the app's own MPU-6050 (Adafruit_MPU6050.h and MPU6050.h), and a self-balancing robot to build on.

parts.name: Tilt switch (SW-520D module)
parts.description: A tiny ball in a tube: upright (pins down), the ball closes the switch and DO is LOW; tip it more than about 45 degrees and DO goes HIGH. VCC (3.3-5 V), GND, DO. Glue it to something and tilt that, or carry it with the hand and turn it over.

parts.name: Compass (QMC5883L, GY-271)
parts.description: A 3-axis magnetic sensor: it feels the Earth's field, so it knows which way it faces (north is away from you on the bench: the -z direction). I2C at 0x0D. VCC (3.3-5 V), GND, SCL, SDA. #include <QMC5883LCompass.h>; compass.init(); compass.read(); compass.getAzimuth() (0 north, 90 east: the way its +x side, the arrow, points).

parts.name: Accelerometer (ADXL345)
parts.description: A 3-axis accelerometer (I2C at 0x53): it feels gravity (1 g down when still) and every shake. VCC (3.3-5 V), GND, SDA, SCL. #include <Adafruit_ADXL345_U.h>; Adafruit_ADXL345_Unified accel(12345); accel.begin(); sensors_event_t e; accel.getEvent(&e); e.acceleration.x (m/s2). Axes: x along the board, y away from the pins, z up.

examples.name: Self-balancing robot
examples.description: Two wheels and a tall body that would fall over: the board reads the MPU-6050 and drives the motors to keep it upright (a PID loop). Press Run, then push it with the hand (Shift) and watch it catch itself; the serial monitor's Plot shows the angle.

examples.name: Compass and tilt alarm
examples.description: A compass prints which way it faces and a tilt switch sounds the alarm LED. Pick the little board up with the hand: turn it (Q / E) and the heading changes; tip it over and the LED lights.
